target.title: fix(update): keep self-updates on the running install's global root
target.body:
## Summary

- `resolveGlobalInstallTarget` now prefers the global root that the resolved package root lives in for npm targets
- the `npm root -g` probe only decides the target when no package root is known
- a probe result under an ephemeral per-Node prefix (Homebrew Cellar, nvm/n/asdf/volta version dirs) is never adopted, reusing the classifier #93650 added for npm command selection

## What Problem This Solves

Package self-updates picked their install target from `npm root -g` even when the package root the process is running from was already known. If PATH's npm doesn't belong to the running install's Node tree, the probe points at a different global root. The update installs there, reports success, and the install that's actually running stays on the old version. Probably the same failure shape as #98618.

Concrete case from my gateway's update handoff log (2026.5.28 updating to 2026.6.11): the launchd service PATH had Homebrew's bin first and nvm's second, so the managed `openclaw update --yes` ran nvm's npm shim under Homebrew's node. nvm's npm has no builtin prefix config, so it derived its default prefix from the realpathed execPath:

```
"root": "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.1/lib/node_modules/openclaw",
"before": { "version": null },
"global update": ".../.nvm/versions/node/v24.10.0/bin/npm i -g
    --prefix /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.1/lib/node_modules/.openclaw-update-stage-2EAbUE openclaw@latest"
```

`"before": null` means the update created a brand-new tree inside the versioned Cellar directory (which the next `brew upgrade node` deletes) and ran doctor from it, while the running nvm install kept serving 2026.5.28. Doctor then flagged an entrypoint mismatch and re-staged the service plist, compounding the skew.

#93650 already stops the per-Node npm *command* from being used, but the probed *target root* was never validated, and `honorPackageRoot` is only set on managed-service redirects, so the "roots match, but the service environment's npm points elsewhere" case fell through.

## Fix

In `resolveGlobalInstallTarget`, for npm targets:

1. if the package root is known, its own `node_modules` parent is the target (this is where the running install lives, so it's the only tree worth updating)
2. the `npm root -g` probe is a fallback for when no package root is known
3. a probe result whose prefix is an ephemeral per-Node path is rejected outright

When the probe agrees with the running root (the normal case) nothing changes. pnpm and bun targets are untouched. No existing test needed modification.

## Evidence

### Test and gate runs

- `pnpm check` passes
- `pnpm build` passes
- `pnpm vitest run src/infra/update-global.test.ts src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` — 272 passed (3 new tests: Cellar probe rejected in favor of the running root, matching probe still adopted, probe failure falls back to the running root)
- full `pnpm test`: 723/724, the one failure (`extensions/litellm/index.test.ts`) reproduces identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so it's pre-existing and unrelated


### Real behavior proof (redacted live transcript)

Live run on the machine from the incident log, using the PR build packed with `pnpm pack` (plus `@openclaw/ai` packed from the same commit and vendored via an npm override, since it isn't published). The artifact was installed with real npm into an nvm-style tree, its version field set back to `2026.6.9`, and `update --yes` executed under a PATH whose npm derives an ephemeral Homebrew Cellar prefix — the same skew as the incident:

```
$ npm root -g        # under the skewed PATH
/tmp/ocproof4/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.1/lib/node_modules

$ node .../v24.10.0/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js update --dry-run
  Root: /private/tmp/ocproof4/home/.nvm/versions/node/v24.10.0/lib/node_modules/openclaw
  Mode: npm
  Current version: 2026.6.9
  Target version: 2026.6.11

$ node .../v24.10.0/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js update --yes
  ✓ global install swap (561ms)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (4.69s)
Total time: 13.48s

after: package.json in the running tree = 2026.6.11
Cellar root contents: (empty — nothing diverted)
```

The running install's version actually changed in place, and the ephemeral Cellar root the probe pointed at stayed empty. On stock 2026.5.28 the same skew installed a full copy into `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.1/lib/node_modules/openclaw` (`"before": { "version": null }` in the pre-fix handoff log quoted above) while the running install stayed stale. (A trailing `uv_cwd` ENOENT after the success line is the demo shell's cwd being swapped out from under it by the install swap, not an updater failure.)

## Review follow-up

- Scoped package roots (`node_modules/@scope/name`) now resolve through `inferGlobalRootFromPackageRoot` by hopping over the `@scope` segment, with a regression test where a scoped root falls back correctly when the probe is rejected (`657cc2d`).
